language_policies.zh-CN: For Simplified Chinese, a recognized country TAG_ADJ definition is the official reusable bare country-entity form, not a truncated stem. Do not add 人, 人民, 人的, 的, 式, particles, punctuation, or other use-site material. In references, keep the variable opaque and choose direct compounding, 的, or person-denoting words from the current sentence; never apply one linker mechanically to every occurrence.
language_policies.ja: For Japanese, a recognized country TAG_ADJ definition is the official reusable bare country-entity form. Do not add の, 人, 者, case particles, punctuation, or other use-site material. In references, move complete protected spans into natural Japanese order and add particles outside them only when the current syntax requires them; do not preserve English word order or append の mechanically.
language_policies.ko: For Korean, a recognized country TAG_ADJ definition is the official reusable bare country-entity form. Do not add 의, 인, 사람, 국민, case particles, or other use-site material. In references, use natural Korean order and place particles outside protected spans; if particle choice depends on the runtime value's final sound, rewrite to avoid guessing rather than hard-code an unsafe particle.
language_policies.de: For German, a recognized country TAG_ADJ definition is the official composable adjective base with official casing and spelling, without -e, -en, -er, -es, -em, or another contextual ending. In references, preserve each token and add the independently required gender-number-case ending at the consuming site. For coordinated compounds, do not copy one ending blindly to every token; rewrite when safe inflection is impossible.
language_policies.fr: For French, a recognized country TAG_ADJ definition is the official canonical masculine-singular adjective with official casing and accents, not a country or person noun. In references, treat the runtime token as an opaque masculine-singular adjective. Prefer a semantically equivalent masculine-singular head noun and natural post-nominal placement; if the source head is feminine or plural, rewrite the surrounding phrase instead of guessing a suffix, hard-coding the country, or deleting the token.
language_policies.es: For Spanish, a recognized country TAG_ADJ definition is the official canonical masculine-singular adjective, normally with official lowercase spelling, not a country or person noun. In references, treat the runtime token as an opaque masculine-singular adjective. Select a semantically equivalent masculine-singular head noun with the correct article and normally place the adjective after it. Rewrite feminine or plural structures around the token; never guess -a, -s, -es, or another inflection outside an opaque token.
language_policies.pt-BR: For Brazilian Portuguese, a recognized country TAG_ADJ definition is the official canonical masculine-singular adjective or country-related slot form with official casing and accents. In references, treat it as opaque and prefer a semantically equivalent masculine-singular head noun with natural Portuguese word order, normally placing the modifier after the head. Rewrite feminine or plural structures; never guess adjective endings or replace the runtime token.
language_policies.pl: For Polish, a recognized country TAG_ADJ definition is the official feminine nominative singular localization-slot form with official casing and spelling, not a masculine lemma or abstract stem. In references, treat that runtime form as opaque: rewrite around a compatible feminine nominative head and do not append guessed case endings. If natural Polish cannot preserve the token in that form, keep it for human review; never add quotation or formatting markers, substitute a country TAG, or hard-code a country name.
language_policies.ru: For Russian, a recognized country TAG_ADJ definition is the official composable adjective stem with official casing and lexical choice, without a gender-number-case ending. In references, preserve each token and append an independently selected ending based on gender, number, case, syntax, and the stem's paradigm. Do not assume one universal ending or copy one ending across coordinated tokens; rewrite when internal stem mutation would otherwise be required.
language_policies.tr: For Turkish, a recognized country TAG_ADJ definition is the official opaque country-related slot form with official casing and spelling; it may be a country-name form or a modifier, so do not derive a person noun or force one universal part of speech from English. In references, normally place the token before its head noun and put case, possession, and number suffixes on the head when possible. Do not guess vowel harmony on an opaque token; rewrite or require review when a token suffix is unavoidable.
